newsitem.title: JORDAN: Israel's Peres says Mideast peace won't be stopped.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Peres says Mideast peace won't be stopped.

text.p: Former Israeli prime minister Shimon Peres said on Friday that progress towards Middle East peace was irreversible despite the near collapse of Arab-Israeli negotiations in recent months.
"We are now at a crisis of peace, but I don't believe that a single man or organisation, a party or a cabinet can stop the march of this movement," Peres told a U.N. leadership workshop in Jordan.
Peres criticised Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who toppled him in a knife-edge election last year, for promising Israeli electors a "low-cost" peace with no concessions to Palestinians.
But he told his audience of budding world leaders, being groomed at the U.N. workshop in the art of global leadership, that true leaders had to take unpopular decisions.

"In peace you have no alternative to compromise. And who applauds compromises?" Peres said. "Occasionally you have to take the risk of doing not what the people want at the time, even if you lose support."
He cited the 1993 Palestinian self-rule accord he and his assassinated predecessor Yitzhak Rabin reached with the Palestinians -- criticised by Netanyahu as a sellout.
"I don't feel any regrets... We did what we had to do and we knew we were taking risks," Peres said.
"Prepare yourselves to be controversial and don't expect to be popular," said Peres, who was twice prime minister but failed to win outright a national election in five tries between 1977 and 1996.
Peres was addressing a group of 160 budding leaders from around the world, selected for one-month U.N. International Leadership Academy at the University of Jordan.

Students had threatened to protest against his presence in Jordan but there were no demonstrations at the university. Jordanians have voiced growing discontent over their 1994 peace treaty with Israel, which has brought few of the economic benefits they were promised at the time.
Peres, whose own Labour Party denied him the honorary title of party president last month when he was replaced as party leader, said he was not leaving politics.
"This is not the time to quit but to fight. We have revolutionised the situation and we are still in the middle of the struggle," he said.

Israeli-Palestinian talks collapsed in March when Netanyahu's government started building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. The Palestinians want Israel to freeze settlement building before they return to the negotiating table but Israel has so far refused.

Peres, who was scheduled to have dinner with Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali, said his "greatest dream" was to turn the Jordanian frontier with Israel "from a dividing line into (a line) of cooperation."
